entries.reason: the 16.4 SDK declares neither this nor anything else in the multi-image family (its VTDecompressionSession.h ends at CVImageBuffer in the decode callback) and no release this port builds exports it - _VTDecompressionSessionSetMultiImageCallback is absent from the 4.3 and the 6.1.3 armv7 caches - so the port has to export it
entries.effect: noErr, with the callback and its reference value accepted and NOT stored. MEASURED on this host, 2026-10-03, on an ORDINARY single-image H264 session: the host answers 0, so a port that answered an error would refuse a call the release accepts. WHAT DIFFERS FROM THE HOST is named here: the 26.2 header says of an installed callback 'When installed, outputMultiImageCallback will also be used when DecodeFrame operations fail and return a nonzero status', and on the port a FAILING DECODE STILL REACHES THE SESSION'S SINGLE-IMAGE CALLBACK, because the session is the release's and the release's decode output has no multi-image parameter to carry a failure anywhere else. Nothing is stored in a table: an address-keyed process-global table leaks when a session dies and hands a later session at the same address a callback it was never given, and a value nothing reads is not an installation either
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTDecompressionSession.h:388-401 for the declaration and its discussion; the per-band ladder from tools/corpus/dump-cache.lua over ~/.charon/dyld/4.3/dyld_shared_cache_armv7 and the 6.1.3 dump; the release's own decode callback shape is the 16.4 SDK's VTDecompressionSession.h:85-92

entries.reason: the 16.4 SDK does not declare it and no release this port builds exports it (_VTDecompressionSessionDecodeFrameWithMultiImageCapableOutputHandler is absent from the 4.3 and the 6.1.3 armv7 caches), so the port has to export it. What decides it is not the missing symbol but the callback's argument: the handler receives a CMTaggedBufferGroupRef, and the release's own decode callback has no parameter that could receive one
entries.effect: kVTVideoDecoderNotAvailableNowErr (-12913), with the caller's block neither retained nor called and *infoFlagsOut set to 0 because nothing was decoded. The header sanctions the refusal - 'If the VTDecompressionSessionDecodeFrameWithMultiImageCapableOutputHandler call returns an error, the block will not be called' - so the caller sees the refusal in the status instead of a callback that never arrives
entries.source: SDK 26.2, VTDecompressionSession.h:444-480 for the declaration; CMTaggedBufferGroup arrived with iOS 14 and no release the port builds has it, which is the measured cause
